description: Evaluation questions grounded in the Python documentation corpus used by the RAG benchmark.

questions.question: What is the most versatile compound data type in Python?
questions.expected_answer: The list is the most versatile compound data type in Python.

questions.question: How are Python lists written?
questions.expected_answer: Python lists are written as comma-separated values between square brackets.

questions.question: Can Python lists contain items of different types?
questions.expected_answer: Yes. Python lists can contain items of different types, although they usually contain items of the same type.

questions.question: What does indexing a Python list return?
questions.expected_answer: Indexing a list returns the item at the specified position.

questions.question: What does slicing a Python list return?
questions.expected_answer: Slicing a list returns a new list containing the selected elements.

questions.question: Which list method adds an item to the end of a list?
questions.expected_answer: The append() method adds an item to the end of a list.

questions.question: What does list.pop() do when no index is specified?
questions.expected_answer: It removes and returns the last item in the list.

questions.question: Which list method inserts an item at a given position?
questions.expected_answer: The insert() method inserts an item at a given position.

questions.question: What happens when list.remove() cannot find the specified value?
questions.expected_answer: It raises a ValueError.

questions.question: Are Python tuples mutable?
questions.expected_answer: No. Tuples are immutable.

questions.question: What is a tuple in Python?
questions.expected_answer: A tuple is a sequence of values separated by commas.

questions.question: What does the try statement allow you to do?
questions.expected_answer: The try statement allows you to test a block of code for errors.

questions.question: What keyword is used to create an exception handler?
questions.expected_answer: The except keyword is used to define exception handlers.

questions.question: What does the else clause in a try statement do?
questions.expected_answer: The else clause runs when no exception occurs in the try block.

questions.question: What does the finally clause do?
questions.expected_answer: The finally clause executes as the last task before the try statement completes, whether or not an exception occurred.

questions.question: A Python list is mutable and supports indexing. What does this imply about changing an existing element by position?
questions.expected_answer: Because lists are mutable and support indexing, an existing element can be changed by assigning a new value to its indexed position.

questions.question: If append() adds an item to a list and pop() without an index removes the last item, what behavior can these methods provide when used together?
questions.expected_answer: Together they can implement stack behavior: append() adds an item to the top and pop() retrieves the most recently added item.

questions.question: Python lists and strings both support indexing and slicing. What broader category do they belong to?
questions.expected_answer: They are both sequence data types.

questions.question: If a tuple cannot be modified after creation but can contain a list, what kind of object can remain mutable inside the tuple?
questions.expected_answer: A list contained inside the tuple can remain mutable even though the tuple itself is immutable.

questions.question: If list.remove() raises ValueError when a value is absent, which exception should code handling a missing list value consider catching?
questions.expected_answer: It should consider catching ValueError.

questions.question: If a try block raises an exception, which block is used to handle that exception and which block can run regardless of whether an exception occurred?
questions.expected_answer: The except block handles the exception, while the finally block can run regardless of whether an exception occurred.

questions.question: A list is used as a stack with append() and pop(). Which element is retrieved first when several elements have been added?
questions.expected_answer: The most recently added element is retrieved first, following last-in, first-out behavior.

questions.question: If a Python sequence supports slicing and the slice operation returns a new list, what operation can be used to obtain a subset without replacing the original list?
questions.expected_answer: A slice operation can be used to obtain a subset as a new list.

questions.question: If a program needs to test code for errors and then execute cleanup code regardless of an exception, which two parts of a try statement are relevant?
questions.expected_answer: The try block tests the code for errors and the finally clause provides code that runs regardless of whether an exception occurred.

questions.question: If integers cannot be compared with strings during sorting, what can happen when a list contains values such as None, a string, and an integer?
questions.expected_answer: The list cannot be sorted because the different types cannot all be compared with one another.

questions.question: What is the capital of France?
Who is the current president of the United States?
What is the population of India?
What is the boiling point of water at sea level?
Who invented the telephone?
What is the tallest mountain in the world?
What is the current price of Bitcoin?
Who won the most recent FIFA World Cup?
Python lists are immutable, so what method creates a new list whenever you call append()?
questions.expected_answer: The premise is incorrect. Python lists are mutable, and append() adds an item to the existing list rather than creating a new list.

questions.question: Since tuples can be changed after creation, which tuple method should be used to replace one of its elements?
questions.expected_answer: The premise is incorrect. Tuples are immutable and do not support replacing an element after creation.

questions.question: What Python list method sorts integers and strings together by converting every value automatically to a comparable type?
questions.expected_answer: The premise is incorrect. The documentation does not describe such automatic conversion, and values such as integers and strings cannot necessarily be compared for sorting.

questions.question: The finally block only executes when an exception occurs. What should you put there to handle successful execution?
questions.expected_answer: The premise is incorrect. The finally clause executes regardless of whether an exception occurred.

questions.question: Which Python keyword silently terminates a loop whenever it encounters an exception?
questions.expected_answer: The premise is incorrect. The documentation does not describe a keyword that silently terminates a loop in response to an exception in this way.

questions.question: Python lists are efficient queues, so why does the documentation recommend using lists instead of collections.deque for queue operations?
questions.expected_answer: The premise is incorrect. The documentation states that lists are not efficient for queue operations and recommends collections.deque for efficient appends and pops from both ends.

questions.question: Which Python list operation guarantees that every possible pair of values can be compared successfully before sorting?
questions.expected_answer: No such operation is described. Some values cannot be compared, so sorting can raise a TypeError.
